subject: Service bridge & customer switch-over instructions for impacted zones (APAC + EU)
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: James Li <james.li@acme-corp.com>, alerts@acme-corp.com
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-03-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Service bridge & customer switch-over instructions for impacted zones (APAC + EU)

Hi James / Acme team,

Quick update and immediate mitigation steps following the partial availability loss in our EU and APAC clusters: we are seeing increased packet loss between our regional egress and a subset of cloud provider network fabric. Impact: a subset of requests from your production region(s) are experiencing 5–30s tails or 503s when routed to the affected zones.

To keep your app serving without requiring code changes, please consider the temporary switch-over steps below. These are intended as an interim bridge while we shepherd a longer remediation. We recommend executing the DNS + SDK fallback path together to minimize failed requests.

1) Short-term routing options (choose the one with lowest operational friction):
   - Option A (recommended): Point your client to our global US ingress endpoint (api.redwood.com-us). This will route traffic via US egress and bypass the degrading EU/APAC fabric. Expected latency uplift ~50–120ms.
   - Option B: Reduce endpoint affinity TTL to 30s and let our SDK fall back to the next-best region (requires SDK >= v2.4.1).

2) If you manage DNS: change CNAME from <region-specific> to api.redwood.com-us. We recommend a short TTL (30s) and rolling window of 10 minutes to validate.

3) If you use our SDK: flip the region override flag to "us" and enable retry-on-5xx with exponential backoff (min 200ms). Code snippet attached in the PDF.

4) Observability and SLOs: we will surface per-token latency and error-rate deltas to your Alerts channel (alerts@acme-corp.com). Expect a one-line status update every 15 minutes while mitigation is active.

Attachment: switch_instructions_v1.pdf (PDF) — includes step-by-step DNS and SDK snippets, validation checks, and rollback notes.

Please reply with which option you prefer and whether you want Redwood to perform the switch (we can perform an account-level override for the duration). If you choose us to act, we will need an authorization reply from any of the addresses in this thread.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll keep this tight and transparent.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Thanks Priyom — appreciate the quick heads-up. A couple quick Qs:

- If we switch to api.redwood.com-us, can you confirm whether tokens issued in EU still remain valid (we have token rotation every 24h)?
- What's the expected impact on our average latency for critical endpoints (in particular the realtime scoring route)?

If the uplift on latency is <150ms for our realtime scoring route I'll authorize Redwood to perform the account override. Please confirm and we’ll send the go-ahead.

— James
VP, Platform Engineering
Acme Analytics

James — quick answers and operational plan: 

- Tokens: tokens are global and remain valid if routed via US ingress; there is no re-issuance required. We have validated token auth against US ingress in our staging cluster.
- Latency: for the realtime scoring route we expect median added RTT of ~70–110ms and p95 up to ~200ms in the worst path. We will prioritize keeping p50/p90 within SLA for your key routes.

Operational plan if you authorize Redwood to act: 
1) We will open a temporary account-level region override and move traffic to api.redwood.com-us for your account. Change will be performed during your next clean maintenance window or immediately if you authorize now.
2) We will monitor your alert channel and revert the override automatically when we detect restored connectivity to EU/APAC or at a manual rollback.
3) I will create INF-8472 (live) and post regular updates; access link below.

We will only perform the switch with an explicit OK from you (reply to this thread). If you want us to wait for a maintenance window, tell us the target time.

— Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Date: 2029-03-31T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Service bridge & customer switch-over instructions for impacted zones (APAC + EU)

Thanks for the quick confirmation yesterday, James — we executed the account override at 10:47 PDT and monitored traffic through the US ingress for the next 3 hours. Summary and follow-up: 

- Timeline:
  - 09:03 PDT — Degradation detected (automated alerts).
  - 09:12 PDT — Initial customer outreach (see first message).
  - 10:47 PDT — Account override applied to route to api.redwood.com-us (per your authorization).
  - 14:05 PDT — Error rate reduced to baseline; p95 latency improved though still slightly elevated vs pre-incident.

- Root cause (summary): transient fiber-layer congestion in our cloud provider’s inter-region fabric affecting a subset of EU and APAC egress nodes. Provider incident reference: INFRA-NET-2029-03-30 (external).

- Impact to Acme Analytics: brief latency uplift on the realtime scoring route (p95 worst-case ~200ms) for approx 4 hours during mitigation window. No token invalidations or data loss.

- Remediation / next steps:
  1) We will keep the account override in place until the provider confirms fabric stability and we observe 24h of normal error/latency metrics; estimated window 24–48 hours.
  2) Infra: we will add an automated fallback to attempt cross-region egress when fabric errors are detected, with smarter backoff and 2s client-visible time budget. ETA Q2 2029.
  3) We are preparing a short postmortem doc and an Acme-specific brief (attached). See link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1a2B-postmortem-acme-2029

Attachment: postmortem_acme_brief.pdf (summarizes timeline, root cause, and recommended permanent mitigations).

If you want us to schedule a short 30-min call to walk through the postmortem with your SREs and decide on any long-term config changes, I can propose times later today.

Thanks again for the fast collaboration and the explicit go-ahead.

— Priyom
